newsitem.title: INDIA: India's United Front may defer oil meeting again.
newsitem.headline: India's United Front may defer oil meeting again.

text.p: Indian Petroleum Minister Janeshwar Mishra said on Monday the ruling United Front coalition may have to postpone this week's crucial meeting on whether to raise oil prices as he could not attend.

The meeting had already been deferred twice, the second time on Sunday when it was rescheduled from July 2 to July 4. "We are trying to postpone the date because I myself will not be present here on the fourth," Mishra told Reuters.

At its last meeting on June 16, the ruling alliance deferred a decision on whether to raise petroleum prices to plug the government's mounting debt to state oil companies, estimated at 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) at the end of March.

Mishra, speaking after inaugurating a new government office in the capital, said he was trying to persuade the convenor of the United Front's decision-making Steering Committee, Chandrababu Naidu, to postpone Friday's meeting.
Asked when the 15-party centre-left coalition would take a decision on whether to increase the prices of some petroleum products, Mishra said: "I think in the month of July anyhow."
Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram favour raising the prices of some petroleum prices, but they are strongly opposed by leftwing parties in the coalition.
